title: Give the backlog sweep's CPU budget real headroom by cutting what the sweep costs
detail: The full-sweep cost contract in scripts/backlog-contract.test.ts failed PR #5044's test job while every other test passed (2752 files, 29951 tests green; then this one file, 1 failed of 41). The log line: [backlog-budget] guardCpuMs=440040 guardWallMs=116365 probe-cost: n=2421 totalCpuMs=407349 maxCpuMs=5918 slowest=BLD-203. The assertion: check:backlog burned 440.0s of CPU, over its 437.8s budget (2s base + 180ms x 2421 probes). Attempt 2 of the same run on the same sha passed, so the tree did not change: the reading sits about half a percent either side of the line and the runner decides. Two things in that reading say where the cost is. (1) The probes report 407.3s, an average of 168ms each against the 180ms allowance, so an allowance set at 2.3x the average (77ms at n=111) is now 1.07x. (2) The guard's own total is 32.7s above what the probes report, against a 2s base set from a measured 300ms; that gap is CPU the per-probe report does not see, and nobody has attributed it yet. Fix direction, in this order: attribute the 32.7s gap (the guard process at n=2421, and whatever the probes spend outside the node processes that report) and remove it; then convert the most expensive cmd probes to in-process measurements the way LIVE-034 did, starting from the slowest list the sweep prints (BLD-203 at 5.92s is 91 percent of the 6.5s per-probe ceiling). Do not raise BASE_CPU_MS or PER_PROBE_ALLOWANCE_MS: AGENTS.md says fix the cost, not the budget, the constants are pinned by scripts/probes/backlog-cpu-clock.mjs, and ADR-1107 says moving them needs a paired CI and local reading. Each new row adds a probe, so the margin does not recover by itself.

verify.evidence: Fails today: CI run 43890979606 attempt 1 printed guardCpuMs=440040 against a 437780 budget at n=2421 (100.5 percent) and failed the test job. Passes when three CI test jobs in a row on main print a [backlog-budget] guardCpuMs at or under 90 percent of 2000 + 180 x n, with BASE_CPU_MS and PER_PROBE_ALLOWANCE_MS unchanged.
